# Phala Pay

> Self-hosted, open-source, non-custodial crypto payments API for ERC-20 tokens on Ethereum and Base.

Phala Pay accepts ERC-20 tokens on Ethereum and Base: stablecoins such as USDC and USDT, and volatile tokens priced on-chain, such as PHA via TWAP, valued in USD at the quoted price (or, for deposit addresses and mismatched payments, at the price when confirmed). A live (production) route needs commercially licensed price sources. USDC and USDT have commercially licensed price sources; other tokens depend on theirs.

The software is free under Apache-2.0 and takes no per-payment fee. Operators pay for their own Phala Cloud instance, two RPC providers per chain, backup storage, and sweep gas. Payers pay network fees.

Deposit addresses are forwarder contracts that can only pay the merchant's treasury. The merchant sets it with a signed message, and sweeps and refunds from its own wallet or Safe. The service holds no funds and sends no transactions.

Credit arrives in about 7 seconds on Base or 30 seconds on Ethereum, confirmed by a second RPC provider and watched to finality. Signed webhooks update the merchant's ledger. The service runs in an Intel TDX confidential VM with verifiable attestation.

Examples include top-ups and credits for apps and platforms, such as AI APIs, cloud, and compute. There is no public hosted service: each operator runs its own instance on its own Phala Cloud workspace. Phala runs an instance only for Phala Cloud.

Phala Pay is pre-1.0 and has not had a third-party security audit. The live demo uses test tokens on Sepolia and Base Sepolia.
